name: Depression-Era Wacky Cake
description: A one-bowl (or rather, one-pan) chocolate cake with no eggs and no dairy, mixed and baked in the same dish. Swap the water for cold coffee for a deeper flavor.

bakersNotes.commonMistakes: Skipping the wells and dumping everything in at once — the vinegar needs to hit the baking soda directly to get its full lift.
bakersNotes.makeAhead: Best baked fresh, but the dry mix (flour, sugar, cocoa, soda, salt) can be pre-measured and stored airtight for weeks.
bakersNotes.storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3 days — it's an oil cake, so it stays moist longer than a butter cake.
bakersNotes.freezing: Freezes well for up to 2 months, wrapped tightly; thaw at room temperature.

substitutions.flavorImpact: Nearly identical — both just activate the baking soda; a faint citrus note is barely noticeable.

substitutions.replacement: Omit and add 2 extra tablespoons of flour
substitutions.flavorImpact: Loses the chocolate flavor entirely — becomes a plain vanilla-style wacky cake.
Richer, more buttery flavor; crumb is slightly denser.
substitutions.difficultyNote: Slightly harder — butter must be melted and cooled first so it doesn't cook the batter.

name: 3-Minute Microwave Mug Cake
description: A single-serving chocolate cake mixed and baked in a mug, ready before the kettle would've boiled.

bakersNotes.commonMistakes: Overmicrowaving — even 30 extra seconds turns it rubbery and dry. Pull it as soon as the top looks set.
bakersNotes.makeAhead: Not really make-ahead by design — it's meant to be mixed and eaten in one sitting.
bakersNotes.storage: Best eaten immediately; it toughens quickly once cool.
bakersNotes.freezing: Doesn't freeze or reheat well — the texture doesn't survive a second microwave pass.

substitutions.flavorImpact: Noticeably less rich and slightly less tender, but still works in a pinch.
Won't rise properly and will be dense and flat rather than fluffy.
substitutions.difficultyNote: No change, but results are noticeably worse.

substitutions.flavorImpact: Richer flavor, very slightly denser texture.
substitutions.difficultyNote: Slightly harder — needs a few extra seconds to melt the butter first.

name: Yogurt Pot Cake (Gâteau au Yaourt)
description: The classic French kids'-first-recipe cake — you measure everything using the empty yogurt container, no scale required.

bakersNotes.commonMistakes: Overfolding the flour once it's added — this is a tender cake, so stop as soon as the streaks disappear.
bakersNotes.makeAhead: Can be baked a day ahead — the crumb actually improves slightly overnight, wrapped at room temperature.
bakersNotes.storage: Keeps well covered at room temperature for 3-4 days.
bakersNotes.freezing: Freezes nicely for up to 2 months; thaw wrapped at room temperature to avoid condensation on the crumb.

substitutions.replacement: Omit, or a pinch of cinnamon
substitutions.flavorImpact: Loses the warm vanilla background note, but the cake still works.

substitutions.difficultyNote: Slightly harder — butter must be melted and cooled first.

substitutions.flavorImpact: Very similar tang and moisture — barely noticeable difference.

name: No-Eggs Applesauce Snack Cake
description: A moist, eggless spice cake that leans on applesauce for both moisture and binding.

bakersNotes.commonMistakes: Using sweetened applesauce without adjusting sugar — it'll come out overly sweet and slightly gummy.
bakersNotes.makeAhead: Improves after resting a few hours, covered, as the spices settle in.
bakersNotes.storage: Keeps covered at room temperature for up to 4 days — the applesauce keeps it moist longer than most snack cakes.
bakersNotes.freezing: Freezes well for up to 3 months, wrapped tightly.

substitutions.flavorImpact: Loses the warm spice note; still a pleasant, mild snack cake.
Slightly richer flavor, a touch denser.
substitutions.difficultyNote: Slightly harder — butter must be melted and cooled first.

name: Self-Rising Emergency Pound Cake
description: A dense, buttery pound cake that only needs five ingredients if your flour is already self-rising.

bakersNotes.commonMistakes: Under-creaming the butter and sugar — this cake's whole texture depends on that step, so don't rush past 3-4 minutes.
bakersNotes.makeAhead: Tastes better a day after baking once the crumb settles — wrap tightly once fully cool.
bakersNotes.storage: Keeps at room temperature, well wrapped, for up to a week — dense pound cakes hold up longer than most.
bakersNotes.freezing: Freezes excellently for up to 3 months; a classic make-ahead cake.

substitutions.replacement: All-purpose flour + 1.5 tsp baking powder + 1/4 tsp salt per cup
substitutions.flavorImpact: No real difference if measured accurately.
substitutions.difficultyNote: Slightly harder — requires measuring and whisking in the leavener yourself.

substitutions.flavorImpact: Loses the classic buttery pound cake flavor and dense crumb — becomes closer to a regular oil cake.
substitutions.difficultyNote: Easier — no creaming needed, but the texture suffers.

name: Three-Ingredient Condensed Milk Sponge
description: About as close to a true emergency cake as it gets — sweetness and richness both come from the condensed milk.

bakersNotes.commonMistakes: Overfolding once the flour is added — the condensed milk makes the batter dense already, so a light hand matters.
bakersNotes.makeAhead: Best within a day or two of baking — it's a simple sponge without much shelf-stabilizing fat.
bakersNotes.storage: Keeps covered at room temperature for 2-3 days.
bakersNotes.freezing: Freezes acceptably for up to a month, though texture is best fresh.

substitutions.replacement: All-purpose flour + 1.5 tsp baking powder + 1/4 tsp salt per cup
substitutions.flavorImpact: No real difference if measured accurately.
substitutions.difficultyNote: Slightly harder — requires measuring the leavener yourself.

substitutions.replacement: No good substitute — this cake depends on it for both sweetness and structure
substitutions.flavorImpact: Not recommended without it; texture and sweetness would be very different.

name: Lemon Yogurt Drizzle Cake
description: A brighter cousin of the yogurt pot cake, finished with a tangy lemon drizzle instead of frosting.

bakersNotes.commonMistakes: Pouring the drizzle over a fully cooled cake — it needs to go on while the cake is still hot so it actually soaks in instead of pooling on top.
bakersNotes.makeAhead: Can be made a day ahead — the drizzle keeps it moist and the lemon flavor deepens overnight.
bakersNotes.storage: Keeps covered at room temperature for 3-4 days thanks to the syrup soak.
bakersNotes.freezing: Freezes well for up to 2 months; the drizzle crust holds up fine after thawing.

substitutions.replacement: Omit the drizzle and dust with powdered sugar instead
substitutions.flavorImpact: Loses the tangy finish, but the base cake is still moist and pleasant.

substitutions.difficultyNote: Slightly harder — butter must be melted and cooled first.
